risks: Our business exposes us to the risk of disputes with customers, suppliers and other counterparties, which may result in legal proceedings against us under various laws, including the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 (“IBC”) and the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (“NI Act”).

Ltd. 02.09.2019 Dismissed as Withdrawn 07.02.2020 Further, in past certain criminal complaints were also initiated against our Company and Promoters by some of our suppliers under Section 138 read with Sections 141 and 142 of the NI Act, in relation to dishonour of cheques.

Our proposed shifting of manufacturing operations from Delhi to Sonipat, Haryana may involve operational risks and uncertainties which could adversely affect our business, operations and financial condition.
We currently carry out our confectionery manufacturing operations at our existing facility located in Delhi.

We propose to shift our entire manufacturing operations to our facility located at Barhi, Sonipat, Haryana in order to consolidate operations, improve operational efficiencies and support our future growth plans.

However, the relocation and transition of manufacturing activities involve several operational and logistical challenges, and there can be no assurance that such shifting will be completed within the expected timelines or without disruptions to our business operations.

The process of shifting operations requires relocation and installation of machinery and equipment, establishment of utilities and infrastructure, obtaining and maintaining regulatory approvals, transferring production processes, and stabilising manufacturing operations at the new facility.

During this transition period, we may face temporary disruptions in production, delays in installation and commissioning of equipment, challenges in process stabilisation, and interruptions in supply of finished goods to our distributors and customers.

other_material_facts.value: Global Economic Landscape The nominal global GDP growth rate was 4.9% in CY25; expected to sustain growth at a CAGR of 4.7% from CY25 to CY30.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: Between CY20 and CY25, the global economy registered a CAGR of 6.2%, stabilizing after a period of heightened volatility driven by post-pandemic recovery efforts, supply chain realignments, and policy tightening cycles.

other_material_facts.label: industry_evidence
other_material_facts.value: India’s low per capita base presents significant room for expansion, with consumption projected to rise to 0.5 by FY’30E, growing at a CAGR of ~4.6%.

other_material_facts.label: working_capital

other_material_facts.label: working_capital

overview.business_overview:
We are engaged in the manufacturing and marketing of confectionery products in India, with a diversified product portfolio comprising over 300+ SKUs across multiple categories, including choco delights, jellies, baked treats and other confectionery formats. We also manufacture and supply food and bakery ingredients. We focus on developing confectionery products at accessible price points and distributing them across a wide geographic footprint, including urban and semi-urban markets, as well as smaller towns and rural areas.

According to Ken Report, the Indian confectionery market size was INR 93.1 thousand crore in FY’25 and is projected to grow to INR 125.8 thousand crore by FY’30, at a CAGR of 6.3%. The market has demonstrated robust growth, expanding at a CAGR of 9.1% between FY’19 and FY’25, driven by rising consumer demand for affordable indulgences, increased frequency of festive consumption, and deeper penetration of packaged chocolate and sugar confectionery across both urban and rural markets. Confectionery items priced between INR 1–10 accounted for the highest purchase intent at 86%, indicating their dominant role in daily consumption patterns. The Indian confectionery market has seen a significant transformation, driven by the shift in tastes of urban and semi-urban consumers. Small-pack, low-cost options priced under INR 10 have penetrated Tier 2/3 cities, making innovative flavors and textures more accessible. India’s economy confectionery market was valued at INR 50.5 thousand crores in FY’25, reflecting the continued relevance among price-sensitive consumers, particularly in Tier 2–3 cities and rural areas. India consumed 523.0 million kg of confectionery, with a per capita consumption of 0.37 kg in FY’23, which reached 0.39 kg by FY’25, substantially lower than countries like Germany (14.4), USA (9.1), and Japan (3.2). Despite the low per capita figure, India's absolute population base is driving total consumption reaching 576 million kg in FY’25, positioning it as a high-volume yet under-penetrated market. India’s low per capita base presents significant room for expansion, with consumption projected to rise to 0.5 kg by FY’30E, growing at a CAGR of ~4.6%. This growth is being driven by urbanization, rising incomes, a young population, and increasing access to affordable SKUs.

We market our consumer products under two brands, “Hugs” and “Tosca”. Under our flagship “Hugs” brand, we offer products across four categories, including baked treats, choco delights, jellies, and panned and sugar confectionery. The “Hugs” portfolio is largely positioned at mass-market price points, with a majority of products priced at ₹10 or below. According to the Ken Report, 68% of non-adult consumers opt for confectionery, including chocolate, at price points of ₹10 or below. Confectionery products are typically impulse-driven purchases, and sales are influenced by product availability and visibility at retail points. According to the Ken Report, 92% of grocery consumption in India continues to occur through Kirana stores. As on March 31, 2026, our products are distributed through a network of over 300 super stockists and are available across kirana outlets in around 24 states in India. Our distribution model is focused on driving volumes through repeat purchase-driven SKUs and wide retail penetration.

Under our “Tosca” brand, we offer products with a relatively higher unit selling price, positioned towards mass-premium segments. The brand is currently being developed with a focus on e-commerce and quick commerce channels. The “Tosca” portfolio comprises products with differentiated formats and packaging targeted at urban consumers. We are also expanding the “Tosca” portfolio to include products incorporating cereal-based ingredients, aligned with evolving consumer preferences for differentiated snacking options. As part of this portfolio, we formulated “Tosca Oat Choco”, an oat and cereal-based bar positioned as an alternative to traditional confectionery formats, containing approximately 33% less sugar than certain leading chocolate bars, based on internal product comparisons.

In addition to marketing and sales of consumer products under our own brands, we also undertake private label manufacturing for third-party customers. We also export our products to international markets, including countries in the Middle East, South Asia and Europe. These channels complement our core consumer business and support diversification across customers, product formats and routes to market.

We focus on product development and innovation as part of our business operations. In the confectionery industry, the introduction of new products and variants is an important aspect of maintaining relevance with evolving consumer preferences. We have a team of food and packaging technologists engaged in developing new products, improving existing formulations and working on packaging formats. Our product development efforts are aligned with market requirements and informed by consumer preferences across different age groups and consumption occasions. This supports the introduction of products across multiple price points. We continuously introduce new variants, flavours and packaging formats across our portfolio, including products incorporating different ingredient combinations.

Our manufacturing operations are supported by production facilities located in Delhi and Sonipat, Haryana. The Sonipat facility is being developed as part of the consolidation and expansion of our existing Delhi operations, with the objective of increasing production capacity and supporting future growth. All our consumer products are manufactured in-house, enabling us to maintain control over product quality, processes and timelines. Our operations are supported by machinery sourced from multiple countries, including Turkey, China and Indonesia, along with ancillary equipment from domestic suppliers, enabling us to support production across a wide range of SKUs. We follow defined processes across procurement, production and packaging, supported by quality assurance systems aimed at maintaining consistency in product quality. For the three months period ended June 30, 2026, our revenue from operations, EBITDA and net profit were ₹4,724.10 lakhs, ₹852.32 lakhs and ₹407.88 lakhs, respectively. For the Financial Years 2026, 2025 and 2024, our revenue from operations was ₹19,261.52, ₹18,697.32 lakhs and ₹16,241.26 lakhs, respectively. Our CAGR for revenue from operations is 8.90% from Fiscal 2024 to Fiscal 2026. For the Financial Years 2026, 2025 and 2024, we recorded EBITDA of ₹3,014.81 lakhs, ₹2,278.70 lakhs and ₹1,893.66 lakhs respectively. Our CAGR for EBITDA is 26.18% from Fiscal 2024 to Fiscal 2026. For the Financial Years 2026, 2025 and 2024, our net profit was ₹1,337.05 lakhs, ₹830.20 lakhs and ₹525.45 lakhs respectively. Our CAGR for net profit is 59.52% from Fiscal 2024 to Fiscal 2026.

We are led by an experienced promoter–management team with domain knowledge in the food processing industry. Our Promoter, Kapil Garg, has over two decades of experience in the consumer-packaged food industry and has been associated with our business since inception. Under his leadership, our Company has scaled its operations and expanded its product portfolio and distribution network across India. He is involved in overseeing the overall strategy of the Company, including business development, product portfolio expansion and operational planning.
